stable.label: iOS 27.2
stable.notes: Current build for every iPhone that can run iOS 27. iOS 27.1 never reached regular iPhones: it was exclusive to the iPhone Duo (23 Oct). Press coverage of Apple's notes says 27.2 patches 160+ security vulnerabilities, adds Siri AI languages (French, Korean, Japanese, Spanish, Portuguese) on supported iPhones, and adds Suggestions in Messages and Shared Albums in Photos. The supported-device list did not change.

upcomingFeature.label: iOS 27.2.1
upcomingFeature.notes: Small bug-fix/security update that MacRumors spotted in its visitor logs on 2 Nov; Apple appears to be testing it internally. No release found as of 6 Nov and Apple has not published contents or a date, so timing is a guess.

beta.label: iOS 27.3 (beta)
beta.notes: Developer beta 1 arrived 3 Nov and public beta 1 on 5 Nov. It brings back the redesigned Health app and, in China, the first Apple Intelligence features (iPhone 15 Pro and later). Apple says the final release is due in December, with no exact date. Not recommended on a main iPhone.

communitySentiment.label: Stable: 27.2 is current, 27.2.1 fix-up on the way
communitySentiment.summary: iOS 27 launched 14 Sep and 27.0.1 (28 Sep) fixed the main launch bugs. Apple never shipped 27.1 to regular iPhones, so iOS 27.2 (26 Oct) is the next update for everyone and reportedly carries 160+ security fixes plus more Siri AI languages. Apple is already testing a small 27.2.1; the coverage reviewed showed no widespread 27.2 problems, though that is not proof none exist. A temporary battery dip after updating is normal. Siri AI remains limited to iPhone 15 Pro and later.
communitySentiment.sourceNote: MacRumors, 9to5Mac, iClarified and press summaries of Apple's release notes (as of 6 Nov 2026). Reddit and YouTube were not sampled for this refresh.

updateProbability.label: Safe to update. Aim for 27.2 (security fixes); 27.2.1 is coming soon

breakdown.note: 27.2 (26 Oct) is the current build for all supported iPhones; 27.2.1 is already in testing.
No widespread 27.2 regressions in the coverage reviewed on 6 Nov; absence of reports is not proof.

adviceByTier.ai: Update to 27.2 now for the expanded Siri AI languages and a large security patch set.
adviceByTier.mid: 27.2 is a sensible update; low risk on A16-class chips, and the security fixes alone justify it.
adviceByTier.entry: Supported, and worth installing for the security fixes. On older chips you can wait a few days for 27.2.1 if you prefer a single stable jump.

ios.pointReleaseAdvice: If you are on 27.0 or 27.0.1, move to 27.2: it is the current build for all supported iPhones (27.1 was iPhone Duo-only). A small 27.2.1 is in testing, so if you want to avoid a brand-new build you can reasonably wait a few days for it.

stable.label: Android 17
stable.notes: Stable on Pixel since June; QPR1 (the September Feature Drop) is stable on supported Pixels. Samsung's One UI 9 (Android 17) is rolling out in waves: Fold8/Flip8 and Galaxy S26 first, then S25 and Fold7/Flip7 (late Sept), S24 and Fold6/Flip6 (6 Oct), and budget/mid-range A- and M-series from 30 Oct. OnePlus, Xiaomi, OPPO and vivo/iQOO builds are expected from about November.

upcomingFeature.label: Android 17 QPR2
upcomingFeature.notes: Next Pixel Feature Drop, expected in December 2026. It will not come to the Pixel 6 or 6 Pro, which have reached end of life.

beta.label: Android 17 QPR2 (beta)
beta.notes: Latest beta I could confirm (a small fix release on 16 Oct). It covers the Pixel 6a through the Pixel 10 series and the Pixel 11 series. Final release is targeted for December. Not for daily drivers.

communitySentiment.label: Mature on Pixel; Samsung One UI 9 rollout widening
communitySentiment.summary: Android 17 and QPR1 are stable on supported Pixels, and the Pixel 11 series launched on Android 17 in August. One UI 9 has reached the Galaxy S26, S25 and S24 families and Fold/Flip 6 to 8; budget and mid-range Galaxy A/M models began on 30 Oct. Some S24 and S25 owners report fast battery drain after One UI 9; so far these look isolated and Samsung has not acknowledged a bug. Pixel 6 and 6 Pro have reached end of life (final patch in October).
communitySentiment.sourceNote: Android Developers release notes, Droid Life, 9to5Google, Android Authority, SamMobile (as of 6 Nov 2026). Reddit and YouTube were not sampled for this refresh.

updateProbability.label: Safe on Pixel and Samsung flagships; budget/mid-range OEM builds are only starting

adviceByTier.flagship: Install when your OEM posts a stable build. Pixel and Galaxy flagships have had Android 17 for weeks, and One UI 9 is out for the S26, S25 and S24.
adviceByTier.mid: Worth updating for security. Samsung A- and M-series builds only began on 30 Oct, so waiting 3 to 7 days for early reports is sensible.
adviceByTier.budget: Prioritise the latest monthly security patch even if the Android 17 build isn't offered yet, and check whether your device is still supported.

android.pointReleaseAdvice: On Android, monthly security patches often matter more than jumping to the newest major version immediately. After a major OEM skin update, waiting a few days for hotfix reports is sensible. Pixel 6 and 6 Pro are out of support after October 2026, so plan a replacement; the Pixel 6a is still on Google's current support list.
